LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 13.3.1 SENTENCES: SIMPLE SENTENCES

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.3: Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Simple Sentences
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Simple Sentences, part of Strand 13 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: What is the role of sentences in a text? 2. What constitutes a simple sentence? 3. How do you determine what to include in a sentence?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Simple Sentences together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and collaboration are improved as the learner speaks clearly and effectively by making points in a logical order.

Values:
Responsibility is enhanced as the learner takes up the task of writing a short dialogue using simple sentences.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Self-esteem is nurtured as the learner ably writes a short dialogue using simple sentences and shares it with peers online and off

line.

Link to other subjects:
